subject: Edge finishing and assembly quality
hook: How should I mark edges on my cutting list?
fb:
Trade question of the week: "What's the best way to mark edges on a cutting list?"

Keep it simple and consistent. On every line, give length, width, quantity and the board décor. Then state which edges get banded and in what thickness: 0.4, 1 or 2 mm. Put length and width in the same order every time so there's no confusion about which edge is which.

If you're not sure, send us a quick sketch of the unit alongside the list. We'd rather check it with you before cutting than have you waiting on remakes.

gbp:
How should I mark edges on my cutting list?

For each panel, give the length, width, quantity and board décor. Then state which edges are to be banded and the ABS thickness for each: 0.4, 1 or 2 mm. Keep length and width in the same order on every line, so edges can't be misread.

If you're unsure, include a simple sketch of the unit. SUPERIO will check the list with you before anything is cut.
